node: Sulphur and sulphuric acid feedstock for copper SX-EW and nickel HPAL
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded US-listed universe for the sulphur/sulphuric-acid feedstock node. The most direct public-market exposures appear to be copper leach/SX-EW operators and nickel HPAL-linked asset owners that are acid buyers, plus a smaller discovery lane of copper ISR/leach developers whose economics may be unusually sensitive to acid availability and logistics. The key evidence input is Kpler's June 2026 report describing China's sulphuric acid export ban, sulphur route disruptions, Chilean copper SX-EW exposure, and Indonesian HPAL nickel pressure. Company-specific exposure still needs verification from filings, technical reports, and procurement disclosures. Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint. The most direct public-market exposures found in this pass are not pure copper or nickel producers, but chemical distributors, sulphuric-acid logistics/merchant-acid platforms, phosphate producers with large acid/sulphur requirements, and copper miners whose SX-EW output depends on acid availability. The underfollowed lane remains evidence-light and needs verification of contract exposure, regional storage, net seller versus net buyer status, and whether acid tightness improves margins or creates cost pressure. Underfollowed expansion for the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint points to a two-lane universe: one reference copper SX-EW buyer to anchor the constraint, plus smaller or messier public-market exposures in SX-EW copper start-up risk, industrial acid distribution, and bulk-liquid logistics.
